1910, Salisbury Plain. Winston Churchill on horseback with General French at the Salisbury Plains in 1910 for the Grand Manoeuvres. Property of the Oxfordshire Yeomanry Trust. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
A Book of poetry, For this Alone, written in camp by RAF POW R.P.L. Mogg and illustrated by a fellow POW. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

A fragment of a First World War Zeppelin and engine starting handle – The airship was brought down over Essex on 24th September 1916. The items come from either of Zeppelins L32 or L33. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

A group photograph showing officers, including Winston Churchill, of the Queens Own Oxfordshire Hussars and other regiments, probably at Blenheim in 1901. Winston Churchill is wearing a slouch hat and bow tie- his Boer War uniform as a member of the South Africa Light Horse. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

Begbie Oil Signal Lamp – The Begbie Signal Lamp came into use in the 1880’s. It has a powerful lens to focus the beam and a shutter operated by a knob on top of the lamp. The operator pointed the lamp towards the next signal station and flashed his message in the Morse code by working the shutter. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
BSA Parabike, 1940s, used by British airborne troops. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Bison Hoof Double Snuff Box, made in Sheffield in 1876. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
‘Boyau 38’ World War 1 French Trench Sign – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

Cold War Tythe Radio -The set is a good illustration of the ingenuity of the technical support provided to the security services that was way ahead of generally available technology of the time. Such efforts played a major part in keeping the UK safe during a very dangerous period of the Cold War. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Framed Cartoon of Lord Roberts and Other British Commanders in the South Africa War circa 1899 – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

The original ‘D’ Squadron, Queen’s Own Oxfordshire Hussars, Headquarters sign that accompanied them throughout the First World War. The reverse has been painted to look like a Public House (Pub) sign for ‘Ye Banbury Arms’, by an unknown artist. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Draft QOOH D Squadron Leaving Cornmarket Oxford For Active Service – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Five Silver Engraved Rum Cups With Leather Case – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
German ‘Coal Skuttle’ Helmet – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

German ‘Pickelhaube’ Spiked Helmet – ‘Pickelhaube’ translates roughly to ‘point’ or ‘pickaxe’ (Pickel) and ‘bonnet’ (Haube). It was also used by fire-fighters and police in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Going to HH The Kings Court with the Hon H Lygon 1910 – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Harold Lambourn Personal Items – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

Horsa Airspeed Glider drawing – The Horsa Glider was designed by Airspeed and to carry a load of about three tons such as a jeep and a light artillery piece or trailer, or a platoon of twenty-eight infantrymen. The Horsa was towed by a heavy bomber or a Dakota transport plane. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

A wooden mannequin, “Jolly Boy”, a piece of dowelling fixed to his back and made to dance on a flat piece of wood.This belonged to Private T. A. Franklin, Queen’s Own Oxfordshire Hussars. At times when morale was low he would entertain his fellow soldiers with “Jolly Boy” by singing. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Letter, photographs and Field Service cap of Private Thomas Alfred Franklin. C. 1918. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Models of Deddington buildings c.1939-45 used by Deddington Air Raid Precautions (ARP). – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Officers Photographed Outside Blenheim Palace – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

Oxford Hussars Football Match Poster – The Queen’s Own Oxfordshire Hussars was the first regiment to play polo in France, and though at first they had to play on very rough pastures, and generally only two-a-side, they got a lot of fun out of it. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Oxford Hussars Lt Churchill in Full Dress – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

Photograph Of A Tent Inspection – A photograph showing an annual tent inspection in progress, this taken at the Queen’s Own Oxfordshire Hussars annual camp held in the grounds at Blenheim Palace, Woodstock, Oxfordshire. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Private H. Lines’ Personal Razor (Boer War) – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Star Objects – Waterloo – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

‘Pte Henry Fisher’ World War 1 Dog Tag which had an eight-sided green tag and the second was a round red tag. In the event of death the red tag was cut off, leaving the green tag on the body. Others finding a body with only the green tag would know that the death was already being reported. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

John Player Cigarette Cards – Showing a portrait of Queen Adelaide who conferred the title ‘Royal’ on the Oxfordshire Yeomanry,saying that ‘the Queen will ever entertain a grateful recollection of the loyal attachment to Her Majesty’s person shown by this fine corps’. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

Specially Bound Copy Of Adrian Keith-Falconers Book. Major Keith-Falconer served with the Queens Own Oxfordshire Hussars and wrote this very important history of the Hussars in the Great War. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
Telescopic sniper rifle sight c.1944 (No. 32 scope for the Lee Enfield No. 4T) – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
The Pearson Cup: Indian 19th Century Hunting Scene Engraved Silver Bowl – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum

Wanted List of EOKA Terrorists – In the Cyprus Emergency from 1955-9 the British Army was called upon to undertake Internal Security duties. Soldiers were issued with a poster showing photographs of suspects of EOKA – the “Nationalist Organisation of Cypriot Fighters”. – Soldiers of Oxfordshire Museum
